items.title: The tradies taking a chance at getting rich quick
items.description: "Escape the 9-5" content is blowing up on social media, but people who have gotten caught up in it warn of the costs.

items.title: One Nation didn't just win. The Liberal vote collapsed spectacularly
items.description: Drafting Barnaby Joyce created a permission structure that has allowed conservative or swing voters to support One Nation: if the bloke who was deputy prime minister thinks the Coalition has lost its way, something in the system must be broken.

items.title: A tropical tax paradise sells much of Australia's gas
items.description: Amid renewed debate over whether Australia is getting enough tax from its gas exports, an investigation by the ABC shows how resource giants use shell companies to shift profit.

items.title: Live: Trump calls Iran's response to peace proposal 'unacceptable'
items.description: Donald Trump rejects Iran's response to a US peace plan as "totally unacceptable" as drone attacks target Gulf Arab nations. Follow live.

items.title: Iran's response interrupts Trump's tee times, meme streams
items.description: The constant trading of insults has the region on edge, but the muted response to missile being lobbed points to a different pose, writes our correspondent Matthew Doran.

items.title: The government has missed one idea to get housing back on track
items.description: If it's serious about improving intergenerational fairness and housing affordability in this week's budget, perhaps the federal government should just build some houses.

items.title: $100m plan to use AI to speed up housing
items.description: Artificial intelligence will be recruited to speed up assessments of housing and energy projects waiting for environmental approval, as the government races to build more homes and ward off a key frustration turning voters away from the major parties.

items.title: Everything we know so far about the federal budget
items.description: Budget night features a lot of political talk and policy wonkiness, but the government's plan will impact your financial situation in one way or another, so it's quite important. Here's what you need to know.

items.title: Bondi royal commission to hear challenge to antisemitism definition
items.description: A royal commission sparked by the Bondi terror attack is this week expected to hear from groups who challenge the commission's accepted definition of antisemitism, as well as expert witnesses from the United Kingdom.

items.title: Regulator found sex offender exempt from needing Working With Children Check
items.description: A sex offender serving as the president of a Melbourne charity received an exemption from requiring a Working with Children Check by Victoria's child safety regulator last year.

items.title: The 'humanitarian crisis' engulfing hospitals across the nation
items.description: The number of aged care patients stuck in hospitals has jumped by 35 per cent in less than a year, fuelling fresh demands for the federal government to stem the crisis.

items.title: 'Tokyo is terrified' as Trump prepares to meet Xi while Japan-China tensions flare
items.description: An incident involving a Japanese soldier allegedly scaling the wall of China's embassy in Tokyo a month ago has become a lightning rod in a tension-riddled landscape between China and Japan.

items.title: Australians evacuated from hantavirus-hit ship to land in Perth
items.description: Evacuating the cruise ship will be a long and complex operation that will stretch into the next day, according to Spain's health minister.

items.title: Live: One Nation fielding candidates in Western Sydney after Farrer win, Joyce says
items.description: One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce says the right-wing party will be shifting its attention to Western Sydney after its historic win at the Farrer by-election on Saturday. Follow live.

items.title: 'We were weird': Tim Finn on Split Enz's rise
items.description: Over half a century later, the band still reigns as one of the most influential and impactful entities on New Zealand pop culture — but it wasn't always that way.

items.title: Fashion designers are experimenting with AI, but not everyone is a fan
items.description: As Australian Fashion Week gets underway in Sydney, local and international designers debate the merits and detractions of using AI in the industry.

items.title: Quiz: How much did Michael Jordan's signed Air Nike 1s sell for in 2020?
items.description: From the Tudor period right through to the 21st century, test your knowledge of the past with this week's history quiz.

items.title: Icebreaker's costly refuelling detour could take years to fix
items.description: A costly refuelling saga affecting Australia's Antarctic icebreaker might not be resolved for another three years under most options, internal government documents reveal.

items.title: Live: Wall Street hits new highs while ASX set to slip
items.description: More strong earnings news, demand for AI stocks and positive jobs data drove Wall Street higher. However, the ASX is set to slip today. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Australian plane gave 'critical' information as Russian jets flew over Estonia
items.description: A European official says they'd be "very happy" if Australia deployed the Wedgetail aircraft again, after it played an important role as NATO responded to an incursion of Russian jets over Estonia.

items.title: 'Incredibly concerned': Zero dog fighting-related charges laid in years
items.description: Experts say dog fighting is going under the radar in Queensland following administrative changes to the state's Animal Care and Protection Act.

items.title: Fire service 'not fit for purpose' in regional SA, uncovered report finds
items.description: An ex-fire chief found SA's Metropolitan Fire Service risks being "completely dysfunctional" due to below-minimum training and facilities, according to Freedom of Information documents.

items.title: Netball body suspends woman charged over alleged antisemitic slur at game
items.description: Jewish community leaders say a woman's alleged slur at an under-12 girls netball game in Sydney reflects a troubling pattern playing out on sporting fields.

items.title: An 'outside the square' Bledisloe Cup idea can be a win for Aussie rugby
items.description: Australian rugby lacks a marquee event that captures the national imagination each year, but this could change if a bold Bledisloe Cup proposal gets approval.

items.title: Jay Vine 'lucky' after 'really scary' stage two Giro crash
items.description: Jay Vine's wife Bre takes to social media to express thanks for everyone's support following her husband's sickening fall at the Giro d'Italia.
